Today’s lesson

Today’s lesson

Learning intentions

  • To be able to understand activity networks that include weights (durations) of each activity.
  • To be able to determine the EST for activities using forward scanning.
  • To be able to determine the LST for activities using backward scanning.
  • To be able to calculate and understand the existence of float times for some activities.
  • To be able to identify the critical path and completion time of a project.

Success criteria

  • I can use forward scanning to determine the earliest starting time of activities in an activity network.
  • I can use backward scanning to determine the latest starting time of activities in an activity network.
  • I can determine the float time for activities in an activity network.
  • I can determine the overall minimum completion time for a project using critical path analysis.
  • I can determine the critical path for an activity network.

  1. Do Now · four VCAA questions
  2. APK · one Year 11 question

Key ideas

Key definitions and formulas

Key definitions

Earliest start time (EST)the earliest an activity can start
Minimum completion timeEST at the finish = the longest path
Latest start time (LST)the latest an activity can start without delaying the project
Float timehow long an activity can be delayed
Critical paththe activities with zero float; a delay here delays the project
Shortest path (Year 11)smallest total weight from one vertex to another

Key formulas

ESTEST = EST of predecessor + its durationforward scan: take the LARGEST
LSTLST = LST of following activity − durationbackward scan: take the SMALLEST
Floatfloat = LST − ESTcritical ⇔ float = 0

Shortest path (Year 11)

George lives in Town G and Maggie lives in Town M.
The diagram below shows the network of main roads between Town G and Town M.
The vertices G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N and O represent towns.
The edges represent the main roads. The numbers on the edges indicate the distances, in kilometres, between adjacent towns.
a. What is the shortest distance, in kilometres, between Town G and Town M? (1 mark)
  1. 1Try routesG–J–K–L–M: 30 + 15 + 25 + 30 = 100
  2. 2BetterG–J–N–M: 30 + 50 + 16 = 96
  3. 3ShortestG–O–N–M: 28 + 42 + 16 = 86
  1. ✓AnswerThe shortest distance is 86 km.

Learn · 14D

Forward scanning: EST

Work from start to finish

  • draw a two-cell box at the start of each activity and at the finish
  • activities leaving the start: EST = 0
  • EST = EST of predecessor + its duration
  • several arrows in: take the largest (everything before must be done)
  • EST at the finish = minimum completion time (the longest path)
ESTlargest in
Minimum completion timeEST at finish
D and E: 0 + 3 = 3 (dummy adds 0)
Finish: largest of 3 + 2, 3 + 3, 2 + 2 = 6 hours
Critical path = LONGEST path, not shortest.

COMPLETE · EST forwards, LST backwards

Finding the critical path from a precedence table

A project has six activities as shown in the precedence table and the associated activity network is shown below.
ActivityDuration (days)Immediate predecessors
A6–
B9–
C8A, B
D7A, B
E10D
F12C, E
  1. aComplete the critical path analysis to calculate the EST and LST for each activity.
  2. bWrite down the critical path of this project.
  3. cWhat is the minimum time required to complete the project?
  1. 1ESTA, B: 0. C, D: largest of 0 + 6, 0 + 9 = 9 (dummy)
  2. 2ESTE: 9 + 7 = 16. F: largest of 9 + 8, 16 + 10 = 26. Finish 26 + 12 = 38
  3. 3LSTback from 38: F 26, E 16, C 26 − 8 = 18, D 9, B 9 − 9 = 0, A 9 − 6 = 3
  4. 4CriticalEST = LST: B, D, E, F
  1. ✓Answers
    a
    bB → D → E → F (the dummy is not part of the path)
    c38 days

Forward scanning

Consider the following activity network. The estimated completion times are in hours.
  1. aFind the earliest start time of activity H.
  2. bFind the minimum completion time of the project.
  1. 1StartA: 0; B, C, D: 0 + 4 = 4
  2. 2NextE: 4 + 6 = 10; F: 10 + 2 = 12; G: 4 + 11 = 15
  3. 3Hlargest of 15 (dummy), 4 + 5 = 9, 12 + 3 = 15
  4. 4Finishlargest of 15 + 4 = 19, 15 + 9 = 24
  1. ✓Answers
    a15 hours
    b24 hours

Learn · 14D

Backward scanning: LST, float, critical path

Work from finish to start

  • finish: LST = EST (the minimum completion time)
  • LST = LST of the following activity − its own duration
  • several arrows out: take the smallest
  • float = LST − EST; float 0 → critical
  • critical path: start to finish using only critical activities (there can be more than one)
LSTsmallest out
FloatLST − EST
C: LST 4 − 2 = 2, float 2 − 0 = 2 hours
Critical path: B–E (EST = LST all the way)
A dummy is never written in the critical path.
Cambridge General Mathematics Units 3&4, 14D pp. 695–699 (own words) · Edrolo General Mathematics Units 3&4, 8I pp. 626–627 (diagram)

Worked example 11 · 14D (c–h)
WHAT · read the boxes

Float and the critical path

(Example 11 continued: the completed network.)
  1. cWhat is the earliest starting time for activity H?
  2. dWhat is the latest starting time for activity H?
  3. eWhat is the float time of activity H?
  4. fWrite down the critical path of this project.
  5. gWhat is the minimum time required to complete the project?
  6. hThe person responsible for completing activity E falls sick three weeks into the project. If he will be away from work for two weeks, will this cause the entire project to be delayed?
  1. 1Read Hbox at the start of H: 12 | 16
  2. 2FloatH: 16 − 12 = 4. Zero float: A, D, F, G
  3. 3EEST 3, LST 5: float 2 weeks = the 2-week delay
  1. ✓Answers
    c12 weeks
    d16 weeks
    efloat = 16 − 12 = 4 weeks
    fA – D – F – G
    g18 weeks
    hNo: E has a float of 2 weeks, equal to the delay, so the project is not delayed.

Backward scanning

Consider the following activity network with the earliest start time for each activity filled in. The estimated completion times are in hours.
Find the latest start time of activity B.
  1. 1FinishLST = EST = 24
  2. 2G, HG: 24 − 4 = 20; H: 24 − 9 = 15
  3. 3Bsmallest of 15 − 0 − 11 = 4 (dummy to H), 20 − 11 = 9
  1. ✓AnswerThe latest start time of activity B is 4 hours.

Critical paths and float

Consider the following activity network with the earliest and latest starting time for each activity shown. The estimated completion times are in hours.
  1. aDetermine the critical path(s) of the project.
  2. bDetermine the float time of activity C.
  1. 1CriticalEST = LST: A, B, D, E, F, H

    aA–B–H and A–D–E–F–H
